question.problem:
Suppose we have a population of size $N=75,$ where $80%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Let the random variable ${X}_{i}$ be equal to

$$
{X}_{i}=\{\begin{aligned}1,\,i\text{th member of the population has the characteristic} \\ 0,\,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

for $i=1,…,75.$ Find $P({X}_{2}=0|{X}_{1}=0).$

current_example.problem:
Workers of a small company decided to elect a new union representative. There are $50$ workers, and $60\%$ of this worker population will vote for candidate $A.$ Let the random variable $X_i$ be equal to
![](@asset-0@)
for $i = 1,\ldots,50.$ Find $P(X_2 = 0 | X_1 = 0).$
current_example.worked_solution:
We have a population of size $N = 50,$ and $p = 0.6$ represents the proportion of the population that will vote for candidate $A.$

Therefore:

- The number of members that will vote for candidate $A$ equals

$$
Np = 50(0.6) = 30.
$$

- The number of members that will *not* vote for candidate $A$ equals

$$
N(1 - p) = 50(1 - 0.6) = 20.
$$

We select two members of the population at random. We need to find $P(X_2 = 0 | X_1 
= 0),$ the probability that the second member will *not* vote for candidate $A$ given that the first member will *not* vote for candidate $A$ either.

If the first member does *not* vote for candidate $A,$ we have

$\qquad$ $N - 1 = 50 - 1 = 49$ members remaining, and

$\qquad$ $N(1 - p)-1 = 19$ members remaining that will not vote for candidate $A.$

Therefore,

$$
P(X_2 = 0 | X_1 = 0) = \dfrac{N(1 - p)-1}{N-1} = \dfrac{19}{49}.
$$
